scope: Proposition 8.15 (Equality tangent) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 77. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In addition to Proposition 8.14, suppose the common-kernel family is closed under joint extraction of its fixed quantum offsets and its full marked certificate records, as in Definition 8.2(iv). Suppose its reference internal metrics on fixed collars retain their actual joint law in these extractions. Then a further law has, separately with positive probability, a saturated nonconstant geodesic segment at upper factor C and a rectangular shortcut of ratio at most C −δ0, where δ0 > 0 is deterministic. The shortcut retains its closed rectangular envelope and its endpoints on opposite envelope faces, as in Proposition 8.14(ii). Under local field equivalence and strong confluence, the saturation event can be written for deterministic anchors a0 ̸= a1, rational 0 < t1 < t2 < 1, and a fixed bounded open U as P([t1, t2]) ⋐ U, FU (P(t1), P(t2)) = C(t2 − t1)D(a0, a1), (8.15) where P is the unique fixed-anchor geodesic, parametrized by fractional length. Only the public strong-confluence assertion that a nonempty geodesic subarc contains a segment of a geodesic between points of a deterministic countable dense set is used.
